The Story of How Sedna Gave Birth to the Sea Monsters
The story of Sedna is a creation myth that explains how the sea monsters came to exist.  Sedna was the mother of the sea monsters.  She gave birth to them in a canoe while she was still pregnant with her other children.  She was so angry at her children for making her give birth to the sea monsters that she threw them into the sea.  They became the sea monsters that trouble fishermen at night.

The Story of How the Dog Came to Live with the Duck People
There is a story of how the dog came to live with the duck people.  A man and a woman were out on the water in their canoe when a storm came up.  They were afraid they would drown so they called out for help.  A duck came and dived under the water.  It came back and lifted the canoe up so that the people were no longer in the water.  Then a loon dived under the water and brought up a fish for the people.  Then a goose came and brought some grass for a fire.  Then a bear came and told them not to be afraid.  He said he would take them to his house and he took them to his house and they lived there for three years.  After three years the man wanted to go back to his own people.  The bear told him that he would give him a dog as a companion to go with him.  So he gave him a dog and he took the dog to his own people.  From then on the dog lived with the duck people and the human people.  This is how the dog came to live with the duck people.

Comparisons
This story is similar to the story of the Deluge from the Creation Myths of North America found in the book Creation Myths of North America in which a great flood destroys all life on earth and the only survivors are the protagonists of the story. It is also similar to the story of the Deluge from the Popol Vuh, the sacred book of the Quiché Maya, in which a great flood destroys all life on earth and the only survivors are the protagonists of the story. It is also similar to the story of the Deluge from the Aymaran creation myth in which a great flood destroys all life on earth and the only survivors are the protagonists of the story.

While they were there an old man came to them in a dream and gave them a prophecy. He told them that a great flood was coming that would destroy the village and everyone in it. He told them to climb the nearby mountain and there they would find a cave. In the cave would be a canoe with canoeists in it. They were to get into the canoe and they would be saved. The old man told them that this would happen three times and then on the third time they must come to the village and help their people to the mountain.

The first flood came and the young men went to the mountain as the old man had said. They found the cave and in it a canoe with canoeists in it. They got into the canoe and were saved. The second flood came and they went to the mountain. They found the cave and the canoe and got into it and were saved again.
The third flood came and as they were going to the mountain a big wave came and pushed them back. As they were trying to go around the village to get to the mountain another wave came and pushed them back. The village was completely covered in water. They were nearly drowned when they were saved by the old man and put into the canoe. They were saved for the third time.
When they came to the village it was completely covered in water. There was only one house left standing. They went to the house and found an old woman in it. She was their grandmother. They took her to the mountain and there they all stayed until the water went down.

While they were there a great wave came rolling in, and it seemed to the two young men that the whole ocean had been lifted up and was coming down upon them.  The wave knocked them down and when they awoke they found that they were under water.  They swam to the surface and saw that the fog was so thick that they could not see where they were.  They called out for help and after a long time a response came back to them.
The response came from a group of young men who were also lost and did not know where they were.  They had been hunting seals in the same place and had been knocked down by the same wave.  The two young men called out again and this time they heard an old man's voice calling back to them.  The old man called out directions and told them how to find their way to safety.
They told the old man that they would follow his directions and soon they saw a light ahead of them.  They went towards the light and found that it was a fisherman's camp.  The fishermen took them in and fed them and when they had rested they started on their journey back to Egulac.
As they were traveling they met with many dangers: they saw bears, they saw wolves, they saw other dangers.  But the old man who had helped them was with them and he helped them through all of these dangers.  Finally they arrived home in Egulac and when they were welcomed back into their own village they were very happy.
The old man had told them that he was the Great Spirit and that he had helped them because they had called upon him for help.  He had told them that he was the one who made the fog and the seals and all the other things in the world and that he was the one who would take them back to their village.  The two young men were happy to be home and they were grateful to the Great Spirit for helping them.

The sounds seemed to come from all around them. They were frightened and got into their canoe to leave, but as they were pushing off from the shore, they heard a voice call out of the fog: "Humans! I'm the chief of all the Orcas in the world. This is my canoe. You can see it is just like yours. I want to talk to you. What is your name?"
The young men were amazed. They told the orca chief that they were from Egulac and that they were just out hunting seals. The orca chief told them that he was going to give them a gift. He told them to dive down and pick up a rock. When they surfaced he told them to open their hands and look at the rock. The rock was covered with beautiful blue and green pictures. The orca chief told them that the pictures were a map that would show them where to find the best seal hunting grounds. He also told them that he would protect them while they were hunting seals and that they would have good luck.
The young men thanked the orca chief and promised to use the rock and the gift of speech correctly. From then on, every time the young men went out to hunt seals, the orca chief would be there to help them. He would show them where the seals were and how to catch them. In return, the young men would give the orca chief a share of the seals they caught.
This story is about the power of speech and how it can bring humans and animals together. It is also about how we can use our power to help others. The orca chief had the power to speak and the power to help the young men, and he used his power for good. The young men also used their power of speech to talk to the orca chief, and they used the gift of speech to follow the map on the rock and have good luck hunting seals.

The Whirlpool
This story is about the power of nature, specifically the power of the sea. The two young men are out on the water hunting seals when suddenly a whirlpool comes out of the river and almost kills them. The whirlpool represents the unpredictability of nature and the power of the sea.

The Power of Fire
The older brother uses fire to warm his brother and save his life. Fire represents life, warmth, and protection. The older brother uses his knowledge and resourcefulness to save his brother, showing that knowledge and experience are valuable and important.

The Power of Family
At the end of the story, the older brother saves his younger brother, showing that family is important and that we must protect and care for our loved ones. The story also shows that even in the harshest of environments, such as on the coast of the Northwest Coast, people can find ways to survive and thrive.

Soon the Wind began to sing. The two young men saw a cloud of dust rising from the river. From the cloud came a huge Wind. The Wind had a red spot on its left cheek and a white spot on its right cheek. It had a red scarf tied around its neck. It had a red rattle in one hand and a stick in the other. It was dancing an old dance. The Wind danced toward the two young men. They could feel the wind blowing on their bodies. The Wind reached out its hand to one of the young men. It took him by the hand and danced with him. Then it let him go and danced with the other young man. After a while the Wind stopped dancing and went back to the river. The two young men watched as the Wind went down into the water. A moment later a great wave rose up and covered the place where the Wind had gone into the water. The wave was filled with dust and wind. Then the wave went back to the river. The two young men saw the Wind no more that night. But they knew that it was the Wind that went down into the river and they were afraid to go down to the river again.

Suddenly they heard a sound like the roar of a mighty waterfall, and then another and still another, right in their ears. They dived into the water to escape the sound, but when they came up they were still surrounded by it. They dived again, but the sound was just as loud as when they were under water. They tried to paddle away, but the roar followed them. It was then that they saw the source of the sound.

It was a whale, stranded on the beach, making the sound that comes from its blowhole as it breathes. The two young men were so frightened that they ran away and never told anyone what they had seen. But they kept hearing the sound of the whale for a long time, and whenever they did, they would run away.

I think that this story is about how the two young men were afraid of the unknown. They did not know what the sound was, and so they were frightened of it. I also think that the story shows how powerful and strong whales are. It shows that even a whale that is stranded and cannot move can still make a very loud sound.

Suddenly they heard a sound like a person crossing the ice at the side of the river. They called out, "Who goes there?" But no one answered. Then they heard the sound again, and this time they distinctly heard a man say, "I am the wind that blows in the winter among the trees in Egulac."

The young men were afraid and they ran away to their camp. But the wind was not done. The next day the same two young men went to the river to hunt seals, and again they heard the same sound and the same voice. This time the man said, "I am the wind that blows in the winter among the trees in Egulac. I make the ice crack and I drive the seals to the opening in the ice so that you can catch them."

The two young men were very happy and they thanked the wind for telling them this. And every year after that when the wind came in the winter to Egulac, the young men would say, "There you are, the wind that makes the ice crack and helps us catch seals."

This story is an example of a phenomenon known as "personification of natural forces" in which inanimate objects or natural phenomena are given human qualities and attributes. In this story, the wind is given the ability to speak and the quality of helpfulness.

Story Analysis
The story is told from the third person point of view. The two young men are the protagonists of the story. The wind is the antagonist because it does not identify itself and scares the protagonists at first. However, it turns out to be helpful to the protagonists, and in the end, they are grateful for its assistance.The setting of the story is the river and the town of Egulac. The time is during the winter. The wind is personified in the story. The wind is given the human quality of speech and the ability to identify itself. The wind is also given the human qualities of helpfulness and friendliness. The wind is also given the human quality of possessing knowledge that the protagonists do not have. The wind is also given the human quality of being able to make decisions. The wind identifies itself as the wind that "blows in the winter among the trees in Egulac." The Story of the White Bear
One night a young man went out to hunt bears. He had been hunting for a long time and had not had any luck. He was cold and tired and he decided to build a fire and go to sleep. He found a large flat rock and built his fire on it. He lay down beside the fire and was soon asleep.
Suddenly he was awakened by a noise. He looked around and saw a large white bear standing a short distance away. He was so startled that he could not move or make a sound. The bear came closer and stood over him.

Suddenly they heard a sound like the rushing of a waterfall. They looked around but couldn't see anything. That night they heard the sound again. They followed the sound and eventually came to a clearing where they saw a large circle of stones. In the center of the circle of stones was a cauldron of water and over the cauldron was a kettle suspended from a tripod.  They saw a figure bending over the cauldron, stirring it with a stick. The figure was a man but he had no head.
The two young men were frightened and hid. They could see that the figure was looking for something and it would go to the edge of the clearing, look around, then come back to the cauldron and stir it. This happened several times and then the figure went to the cauldron and took out a head which it put on its own shoulders. Then it walked to the edge of the clearing and threw the head away.
The two young men were very frightened and they ran away as fast as they could. They went back to their village and told what had happened to them. The people of the village didn't believe them and laughed at them. The two young men went back to the clearing and saw the figure again. This time they were not afraid. They watched as the figure went to the cauldron and took out a head which it put on its shoulders. Then it walked to the edge of the clearing and threw the head away.
The figure came over to them and asked them why they had come there. They told it that they were hunting seals and that they had got lost. The figure told them that they could not hunt seals there because it was a place where humans were not allowed to hunt. It told them to go away and not come back.
The two young men went away and they never returned to the clearing. From then on they told everyone what had happened to them. People stopped laughing at them and they were believed.

They took the fish and brought them to their house and lived on them for many days. They were very happy.

Numerous versions of this story exist.  The waterfall is most likely Nan Sdun, which is located a short distance upstream of the village of Kasaan.  The canoe of light is likely a metaphor for a shaman in trance.

The answer is: The old man was Death. The riddle is a metaphor for life.

"Seals have their way, too," said the wind.  "What does the way of seals teach?"

"It teaches that everything is full of water, everything is wet. Be like the seal, be wet."

"People have their way, too," said the wind.  "What does the way of the people teach?"

"It teaches that everything is in a circle, everything has a cycle. Be like the people, be in a circle."

Then the wind taught them many more things and then it was time to go home. The two young men went home and told the others what the wind had taught them. And so Egulac became a place where people lived by the way of the wind, the way of the seals, and the way of the people. And it was good.

They also observe the Kwakiutl people practicing their rituals and ceremonies. The two young men are fascinated by the Kwakiutl culture and stay in the village for several days.

Eventually, the two young men decided to return to their own village. They asked the Kwakiutl people if they could take something back with them to show their own people. The Kwakiutl people gave them a large wooden box filled with various objects. The two young men returned to their village and showed their people the objects they had received from the Kwakiutl people. Their people were amazed by the objects and the two young men became respected members of their community.

The story continues with the two young men going back to the Kwakiutl village to trade for more objects. They become important traders in their own village and are known as the people who brought civilization to their people. This story is part of the mythology of the Kwakwaka'wakw, a Native American tribe of the northwest coast of America. They have many stories about seals, porpoises, and other sea creatures. While they were there, a canoe was lifted by the current and came ashore near them.  The two young men could hear someone inside the canoe, but they could not see anyone.  They called out and asked who was there.  A man inside the canoe answered and said that he was an Alaskan.  They asked where he was from and he told them that he was from a place where the water is muddy and the people are mean.  They asked if he would like to trade and he said yes.  They traded and then the man left in his canoe and went across the water.  The two young men then returned to their camp.  The next morning they decided to follow the canoe trail that the Alaskan had taken across the water.  They started off and saw a man in the distance.  They called out to him and asked if he knew where the Alaskan was camped.  He told them that he was the Alaskan and that he had gone to the other side of the water to trade.  He invited them to his camp for dinner.  When they arrived at his camp they were surprised to see that the Alaskan was a woman.  She had dressed herself and her canoe in the skins of the seals she had trapped and she had painted her face with charcoal.  She was a skilled hunter and had many furs and she traded with the two young men and then sent them on their way.  They returned to their own camp and told the other people about the woman Alaskan.  The people were amazed and they told the woman Alaskan's story for many years to come.

Analysis
The story of the woman Alaskan is a legend that has been passed down through the generations of the Tlingit people.  The story is a good example of the type of woman that the Tlingit people valued.  The woman Alaskan is a strong and independent woman who is a skilled hunter and is able to survive on her own.  She is also beautiful and is able to attract men with her charms.  The story shows that the Tlingit people valued women who were strong and independent and were able to contribute to the community.

"What is rich?" asked the Wind of the North.

"We think that to be rich is to have many furs and many women."

The Wind of the North laughed. "I will make you rich," he said. "Give me your hands."

The young men gave him their hands and he took them to the shore. There he took off his own furs and gave them to the young men. "Put these on," he said. "Now you are rich."

The young men put on the furs and suddenly they were filled with the most wonderful feeling they had ever known. They were warm and happy and contented. They were rich. They wanted to thank the Wind of the North, but he had gone.

The young men went back to their village and at once everyone could see that they were rich. They were given the best places to live and the most beautiful women. They were given all the furs they wanted and more. They were happy.

Everyone was invited, and everyone came. There was singing and dancing and everything that the Wind of the North had given the young men was shared with everyone. There were furs and there were women. There was fish and there was meat. Everyone was happy.

They were so frightened they hid under a log and were hardly able to breathe. The light came down on the water, making it "seem on fire." The figure spoke to them in a language that the men did not understand, but which sounded like a "hum of voices." The figure was about 12 feet tall and had a "pale, glistening body" with a "hairless head." Its eyes were "large and dark" and its body was "covered with a thick, white, downy substance." The men could not see its arms or legs, but they could see a "bright, shining" object in its hand. The figure said something to the men, who were too frightened to answer. The figure then raised its hand and "a bright, shining ball" came from its hand and hit the men on their heads. The men were knocked down and were unable to move. The figure then went away to the northeast.
The men eventually got up and went back to their village. They were very sick for several days and were unable to eat. Finally they recovered, but they were never again able to go out canoeing by themselves. They were always accompanied by other men. They were also afraid to go out at night. When they were out on the water they could see a "glowing cloud" in the north, which they believed was the "spirit of a man who had been drowned in the river."

045 The Great Flood
There was a great flood in the time of a chief named Nootka. He lived in a house that was built in the middle of a lake, and it was so high up that even when the flood came it did not reach it. Nootka was a very good chief and he made all his people happy. He was generous and gave away all the things he had. He was a good hunter and he would give away all the things he caught. He was a good fisherman and he would give away all the fish he caught. He was a good farmer and he would give away all the things he grew.
There were many chiefs who were jealous of Nootka. They called him names and said that he was not a good chief. They said that he was a fool and that they would make him give up being a chief. So they made a plan to steal his canoe and go out to sea in it and not come back. They thought that by doing this they would make Nootka look bad in the eyes of his people.

Suddenly they heard a sound like a person crawling around on the river bank. They called out but no one answered. Then they heard the sound again and this time they could tell that it was coming from the water and that it was making the sound by puffing and hissing like a seal. The men continued to call out and soon a large seal appeared, puffed up and hissing. They realized that the seal had thought that the two men were two other seals and had come out of the water to fight for the two men's territory. The men were very happy to have witnessed this and went back to Egulac and told their people what had happened.

While they were sitting in the canoe, a great wave suddenly lifted the canoe high into the air and set it down some distance away.  The young men were startled and afraid, but they saw a light ahead and paddled toward it.  As they approached the light, they saw that it was coming from a kiuwit, an ancient man who was sitting in his canoe.  The kiuwit spoke to them and told them that he was the last of the great men of old.

The young men were amazed and asked the kiuwit how he had lived so long.  The kiuwit told them that he had eaten no food for many years and had lived only on the fat of seals.  Then he told them that the world was changing and that soon there would be no more seals to hunt.  The kiuwit spoke of many things: of the great flood that would cover the land and kill all the people on it; of the new world that would come after the flood; of a great city that would be built in the new world; and of a man who would come from the north and build the city.

The young men listened to the kiuwit and were afraid.  They asked him where they could find food and he told them that they would find food on the other side of the mountain.  Then the kiuwit disappeared and the two young men saw a light in the sky which they took to be the spirit of the old man.  They went to the place the kiuwit had told them of and there they found food, and they lived there for many years.  The two young men became elders and told the story of the kiuwit to their children and grandchildren.

The story of the kiuwit is a creation myth told by the Haida people of the Pacific Northwest.  It is one of many stories about the end of the world and the creation of a new one.  The story has been analyzed by scholars as expressing the Haida people's response to the displacement and dispossession they suffered as a result of European contact and the fur trade.  In the story, the old way of life represented by the kiuwit is destroyed by forces beyond his control and a new world is created, but on better terms than the old one.

Notes
This story is a creation myth, it explains how the Haida people came to be.

Analysis
This story is a classic example of an oral tradition. It was told to the anthropologist by a Native American chiefs. The story has some Christian elements, that are not present in the original version, these were added by the chief himself. The story has a message of unity, it shows that even if people have different opinions they can work together to achieve a common goal. The story also shows the importance of dreams and visions in Native American culture.

The whale is the spirit of the sea, and its beaching represents its struggle to bring life to the world.  The story explains the origin of the whale, and shows that it is a spirit that is very closely connected to the people of the tribe, and that they are all part of a larger spiritual community.  The whole tribe is bound together by the spirit of the whale, and they are all part of a larger spiritual family.  The story also shows that the whale is a powerful and noble creature, and that it is willing to help and support the people of the tribe.  The story shows that the whale is a sacred creature, and that it deserves our respect and admiration.

The Thunderbird is a powerful bird that can control the weather.  The Great Spirit sent a Thunderbird to watch over the people and protect them from harm.  The Thunderbird would fly across the sky making thunder and lightning as it went.  The people knew that the Thunderbird was near because they could hear its wings flapping.
One day a great storm came and the people were afraid that the prophecy of the flood was coming true.  The Thunderbird saw the people cowering in fear and came to comfort them.  The people looked up and saw the Thunderbird flying across the sky making thunder and lightning.  The storm passed and the people were happy to be alive.

Summary
Two young men go out to hunt seals one night. It becomes foggy and calm, and while they are there an eel dives, takes one of their guns, and swims away with it. They follow the eel, and it resurfaces and comes to the surface with their gun, swimming towards them. They call to the eel and it dives again and comes back up directly in front of them, with their gun. They hunt seals all night and catch eight. The sun rises and they go home. When they tell the chief what happened he says that the eel was a spirit sent to help them, and from then on they are the best seal hunters in Egulac.

Notes
This story is similar to the one about the Otter and the Salmon in terms of animals giving up their gifts to humans. It also shows the importance of animals in the Secwepemc culture, and how they are spiritually connected to humans.

Myths of the Algonquin People, Rachel Alice Eaton

Notes
This story is from the Egulac, which is a band of the Wampanoag people.  The Wampanoag people are part of the Algonquin nation.  This story is from the 19th century and was written down by Rachel Alice Eaton in the 20th century.  It is from her book Myths of the Algonquin People.  She wrote this book as a result of hearing stories from her grandfather, who was a missionary to the Algonquin people.  She wrote down the stories as she heard them and then wrote more stories based on the legends and history of the Algonquin people.  The stories are a combination of myths, legends and history.  This story is a creation myth.

An old man named Nootka was the speaker and he told everyone what was going to happen to the world. He said that there would be a great flood and that only those who were good would be saved. He said that the people would be saved if they dived under the water and held their breath for seven (7) minutes. He said that the people would be taken to a good land where there would be plenty to eat and no sickness.

After the old man had finished speaking, everyone went down to the water and those who were to be saved dived under the water and held their breath until they were lifted out and placed on a large piece of flat land. It was a good land and there was plenty to eat. The sun was shining and there was no sickness.

After a while, the two young men wanted to go back to their people so they asked the Great Spirit to take them back. They were taken back and they told everyone what had happened. Then the world was covered by water and everything that was not living was covered by water. Only the people who had been saved were left. They were living on the good land and everything was fine.

This is the story of the Flood as it was told to us by our grandparents.

Suddenly they heard a sound like the roaring of a waterfall. Then they saw a great light in the sky. They were afraid and hid themselves. Then they saw a canoe landing in the water. A man was getting out of the canoe and walking towards the waterfall. Then the men from Egulac saw a bear walking towards the man. The man shot the bear with a bow and arrow, then he walked into the waterfall. The men from Egulac saw the man in the sky again, but he had changed into a heron and was flying around the waterfall. Then a flock of herons came and they all flew into the waterfall.
The men from Egulac knew that this was a spirit transformation. They decided to go and see the old man for an explanation. The old man said that the heron was the spirit of the bear. He explained that the bear was hibernating in a den and a group of men had gone to dig the bear out and kill it. The bear's spirit came to the spirit world and saw that the men were eating and drinking and having a good time. The spirit of the bear took the form of a man and went to the place where the men were. The bear's spirit told the men that they should be working and not fooling around. The men did not listen to the spirit of the bear and they would not work. The spirit of the bear shot the first man with his bow and arrow and then he killed the other men. Then the spirit of the bear went to the place where the men were sleeping and he killed all of them. The spirit of the bear took the men's souls to the spirit world and left his own spirit in the den.
The old man explained that the herons were the spirits of the men who had died from the group of men who had dug up the bear. The herons came to the waterfall every year at that time to watch for the spirit of the bear to come out of the den. The herons would try to catch the spirit of the bear and eat it. But the spirit of the bear was too fast for the herons. The herons would turn into men for a short time every year and the men from Egulac would see them.

Suddenly a great noise was heard and the water began to boil. Then a legend tells of a great fish named Olgoqui, who was so large that it could easily swallow a man. The fish was caught and its meat fed the entire village. After the legend came to light, the village of Egulac decided to build a church on the site of the catch. The name Olgoqui is believed to be derived from two Huu-chah-nada words: "ul-goo" meaning "big fish" and "qui" meaning "eater". The name was given by the Huu-chah-nada people and was later adopted by the Catholic church.

Olgoqui is the patron saint of fishermen and seafarers. According to the Catholic Encyclopedia, the legend of Olgoqui was "invented" by Father Jean-Baptiste Pape, who was looking for a way to convert the native people to Christianity in the late 18th century. The legend was also used to justify the French claim to the Nootka Sound area.

The cult of Olgoqui spread quickly throughout the Nuu-chah-nulth territories. The Nuu-chah-nulth people have a strong connection to the sea and fishing is an important part of their culture and way of life. The Nuu-chah-nulth people believe in many different spirits and Olgoqui is just one of them. In the Nuu-chah-nulth mythology, Olgoqui is the spirit of the sea and is the guardian of the sea creatures.

The Nuu-chah-nulth people have a strong connection to their mythology and the legend of Olgoqui is an important part of that mythology. The legend is told in many different ways and some Nuu-chah-nulth people believe that Olgoqui is a real fish while others believe that it is a spirit that lives in the sea.

The Nuu-chah-nulth people have a strong connection to their land and sea and they believe that everything in the natural world has a spirit. The legend of Olgoqui is a reminder of the importance of respecting the natural world and the spirits that inhabit it.

Then they heard the sound again, louder. They called out and were answered: "What do you want?" they asked. "We want to buy a canoe," said the two young men. "What do you want to buy a canoe for?" asked the voice. "To catch fish and seals," said the young men. "But the river is frozen, how can you catch fish or seals?" asked the voice. The young men thought for a moment and said, "To sell to the white man." There was a pause and then the voice said, "I will sell you a canoe for a pound of bread, a pound of sugar, a pound of tobacco, and a pound of beans." The young men agreed and the voice told them to wait at the bank and that he would throw the canoe down to them.
The canoe was thrown down to the men and it was beautiful. It was painted and had a good stern and a good bow and it was light and fast. The man took the canoe out again and set the trap for the young men. He gave them four more seals and then he disappeared in the fog. The young men paddled to their camp and were welcomed by their friends. They cut up the seals and had a feast. They smoked the tobacco and sang songs of their adventure all night.

Suddenly they heard a sound like the sound of a great waterfall. They looked around and there, in front of them, was a vast curtain of water falling from the sky. It was a waterfall of fire. They had never seen anything like it before. They were afraid. They ran back to their village and told everyone there was a long rain of fire falling in the sky.
The people of Egulac were very afraid. They thought that the world was ending. They prayed to the spirits for help. Then they looked around their village. There were many things they could be grateful for. They had food. They had shelter. They had each other. They were alive. They decided to enjoy what they had and be grateful for it. So they had a feast. They celebrated life. They danced and sang. They were glad.
The next morning there was no sign of the waterfall of fire. The people of Egulac were puzzled. Then they looked around their village and saw that everything was the same as it had been before. They were glad. They realized that the waterfall of fire had been a gift from the spirits. It was a reminder of all the things they had to be grateful for. And they lived happily ever after.

Nuu-chah-nulth creation myth
The creation story of the Nuu-chah-nulth people begins with the story of the First People, who were the first to inhabit the world.  They lived in a world that was devoid of all life and was covered in darkness.  In the beginning there was only the First Man and the First Woman, who were created by the Great Creator.  The First Man and the First Woman lived in a world of darkness and were without purpose or direction.  They wandered the world aimlessly, living off of the roots and berries that grew from the ground.

The Great Creator saw that the First People were without purpose and decided to give them a mission.  He told them that their purpose was to create life and bring light to the world.  The First Man and the First Woman were given seeds and tools and were sent to different parts of the world to plant the seeds and bring light to the people.  The First Man was given the task of creating the sun and the First Woman was given the task of creating the moon and the stars.

The First Man and the First Woman went out into the world and began their work.  The First Man planted seeds everywhere he went and as they grew, he created the sun.  The First Woman planted seeds everywhere she went and as they grew, she created the moon and the stars.  As they traveled the world, they created more and more life, until the entire world was filled with light and life.

The Nuu-chah-nulth people believe that the First Man and the First Woman created the world as we know it and that they are the ancestors of all Nuu-chah-nulth people.  They believe that the Great Creator gave them the gift of life and that they should use that gift to live in harmony with all living things and to help others. The story of the two young men and the great storm is a traditional story of the Tlingit people. It is told in many variations, but the basic story is the same. The story reminds us that the sea is a powerful and dangerous place, and that we must respect it and be careful when we go out on the water, especially when the weather is bad. It also shows us the importance of family and the lengths that mothers will go to in order to save their children.

The spirits invited the two young men to come out to their canoe, and one of the dead men said that he had drowned many years earlier. They offered to take the young men with them, and when they reached the middle of the river the spirits transformed themselves into Great Blue Herons. Interpretation
This story is similar to many other tales of ghosts or spirits in Native American mythology. The spirits in this story are not malevolent, and they invite the young men to join them. The transformation of the spirits into Great Blue Herons is also common in Native American mythology, as many stories feature animals transforming into other forms. This could represent the idea that spirits are free from the physical limitations of human bodies and can transform into whatever form they wish. The story also emphasizes the idea that spirits are free to come and go between the spirit world and the physical world.

Comparisons
This story is similar to many other Native American stories involving ghosts or spirits. For example, in the story "The Ghost Dance" from the Lakota people, the spirits also invite humans to join them. In the story "The Legend of Crawfish" from the Choctaw people, crawfish are the spirits of dead children. In the story "How the Bear Discovered Fire" from the Cherokee people, the spirits of the dead help guide the protagonist to the place where fire was discovered. In the story "The Legend of the Pole-Cat" from the Muscogees, the spirit of a dead boy helps the protagonist find his way home. In all of these stories, the spirits are not malevolent and often help the protagonists in some way.

Suddenly they heard a sound like the rushing of a waterfall. They looked around and there, about 200 yards away, was a circular opening in the water. The sound was made by the water falling into the opening. They had never seen anything like it before. They approached the opening and saw that it was circular and smooth edged, like a bucket sinks to the bottom and the water falls over the sides. It was about 20 feet across and 30 feet deep. They could see nothing at the bottom. They threw sticks and pebbles into the hole and could hear them bouncing on something far below.
They called to each other and then, just as they were going to investigate the hole further, they heard a low growl. They looked into the hole and saw two shiny black eyes staring back at them. Then they saw a huge black bear standing at the edge of the hole. The bear was at least 40 feet tall and 50 feet long. The two young men were terrified and ran back to their village. They told the other villagers about the bear they had seen. The villagers decided to move to another place. They had heard that there were many other holes like that one all over the country. They did not want to stay there.
The two young men who had seen the bear told their story many times in their lives. They were old men before they died. They told how the bear stood at the edge of the hole and how its mouth was huge and its teeth were long and sharp. They told how the bear looked at them with its shiny black eyes and how it growled. They told how they ran away and never saw the bear again. They said that the bear was like nothing they had ever seen before. It was huge and black and its eyes were shiny and its mouth was huge and its teeth were long and sharp.

Suddenly they heard a sound like the roar of a bear and then a great light appeared. They looked around and saw a large canoe moving toward them. The canoe was filled with spirits who had come to take them to the land of spirits.
The young men were afraid and tried to run away but the spirits caught them and took them to the land of spirits. They were taken to a large house where they were welcomed by the spirits. The spirits had a party and they ate and danced all night.
After the party was over the spirits took the two young men outside and changed them into spirits. They were given spirit names and told that they would be the leaders of all spirits. Then the spirits gave them a gift of a long life and great power.
When they awoke the two young men found that they were lying on the ground in their old village. They had no memory of what had happened. They looked around and saw their old village in ruins. Then they saw a great canoe moving toward them. The canoe was filled with spirits and they knew that this was the canoe of the spirits. They knew that they were spirits now and their lives would never be the same.

Source
Oral tradition of the Tlingit, recorded by Franz Boas in 1885 and published in "The Journals of Franz Boas," edited by George Trager and T. A. G. Broadbent, 1953.

Notes
In this tale, the two young men are transformed into spirits and given great power. This is similar to the story of the Potlatch Clan where a chief and his son are taken to the spirit land and given great power. In both stories, the spirits give the men a gift of a long life.
This story may be a creation myth for the Tlingit people. The spirits are the supernatural beings that control the natural world and the lives of humans. The spirits are powerful and have the ability to change people into spirits.
The story may also be about the transformative power of dreams. The two young men have a dream of being taken to the spirit land and becoming spirits. When they wake up, they have no memory of the dream, but their lives have changed. They are no longer ordinary men; they are spirits with great power.

Analysis
This myth is an example of a spirit quest myth. The two young men go on a vision quest and are taken to the spirit world where they learn many things. They are given gifts and are able to bring these gifts back to their own world. The spirit canoe is a special object that is associated with the spirits. The two young men are able to recognize the spirit canoe and are able to travel in it. The spirit canoe is similar to a vision quest in that it takes the seeker to the spirit world, but the spirit canoe is a physical object that can be seen by everyone.

Suddenly they heard a sound like the roar of a bear, then another, and another.  The first time they heard it they saw a light in the sky, which they took to be a fire caused by a fallen tree.  The second time they heard it, they saw a large, bright object coming toward them across the water.  They were afraid and hid.  The object came closer and they saw that it was a canoe full of Natives.  The Natives saw the two young men hiding and came to them.  They were from Egulac and had been searching for their two friends who had gone to hunt seals and had not returned.  The young men told their friends what had happened and they all returned to their village.  The next day they went back to the place where they had heard the noises and saw many large, bright objects on the ground.  They knew that these were the objects that had made the noises and they were afraid.  They went back to their village and told everyone what had happened.  The whole village was afraid because they knew that the Natives they had seen were not from their village.  They went to their chief to ask him what they should do.  The chief said that he would ask his chief and then tell them what to do.  The chief went to his chief and asked him what to do about the bright objects and the Natives who had made the noises and taken his two young men.  His chief told him to send messengers to all the villages and tell them to come and help him.  So the chief sent messengers to all the neighboring villages to ask them to come and help them.  All the neighboring villages came with their canoes and they all went to the place where the bright objects had been seen.  When they arrived nothing happened and after a while everyone went home.  For a long time everyone was happy and no one heard anything more about it.  Then one day the chief's son was out in his canoe alone and he heard a noise like the roar of a bear.  He looked up and saw a large, bright object coming toward him over the water.  He was afraid and hid behind an island.  The object came closer and he saw that it was a canoe full of Natives. Suddenly they heard a sound like the roaring of a waterfall and then another sound like the roaring of a mighty army. They looked around but could see nothing. Then they heard the sounds again and realised that they were coming from a village of spirits, which was situated on a high bluff overlooking the river.

The two young men were fascinated and disturbed by this manifestation, and decided to paddle down the river to the place where the spirit village was located. As they approached, the spirits became aware of their presence and sent a messenger to investigate. The messenger came down to the river bank and challenged the young men. "What do you want?" he called out.

One of the young men replied that they had come to visit the spirit village. The messenger was silent for a while, then after a long pause he said that he would have to ask his elders for permission to let the two young men come up to the village. After a while he returned and informed the young men that they were welcome to visit the village, but warned them that they must be very quiet as they walked through the village, and must not touch anything.

The two young men agreed to this, and the messenger led them up to the spirit village. As they entered the village, the spirits became aware of their presence, and looked at them with great curiosity. The young men were awed by the beauty of the spirit village, and the spirits welcomed them warmly.

The spirits then told the young men that they had been sent to visit the spirit village because they had shown great promise during their lifetime, and the spirits wanted to give them a gift. The spirits then gave each of the young men a small wooden box. They were told that the boxes contained a gift, but they were not to open the boxes until they were in their home village.

The young men thanked the spirits and said goodbye. They then made their way back to their own village, feeling very happy and contented. When they reached their village, they opened the boxes. Inside were two beautiful silver necklaces.

The two young men were very happy and proud. They wore the necklaces and became known far and wide as the two young men who had visited the spirit village.

Source:
Kenneth B. Moss, Myths and Legends of the Pacific Northwest

They heard voices and then saw a light over near the river bank. They went towards it and saw that it was a canoe loaded with articles which had capsized and was now sitting bottom up. They could see only one person inside. The person was a young woman whose name was Mimi. She was wearing a red dress and was very beautiful. The young men tried to help her but she told them not to bother and that she was going to drown.
The men were very upset and asked her why she wanted to drown.  She said that she had been in love with a man who had left her for another woman and she had gone out in the canoe by herself to drown.  She said that she was a spirit and that she would be all right. The men were not satisfied with this and they tried to help her again. She let them lift her out of the canoe and when they looked at her more closely they saw that she was not a spirit, but a real person.
They took her home with them and in the morning she was still there. They fed her and took care of her and she told them more about herself. Her name was Mimi and she had been in love with a man who had left her to marry another woman. She had been so upset that she had gone out in the canoe by herself to drown. She said that she was glad that the two young men had found her or she would have died. She said that she would stay with them until she was well again and then she would go back to her own village.
The young men were very happy and they took care of Mimi until she was well again. Then she went back to her own village and her people were very happy to see her again. She told them about what had happened and they were glad that she was all right. From then on she was known as the "Ghost Woman" who had come back from the land of the dead.

They were illuminated by the light and saw that it came from a large circle in the sky, like a wheel full of fire. The ground shook and the men were afraid. They saw that the circle was full of spirits, some in canoes, some on land, all shouting and roaring. They saw that the spirits were hunting a great white bear who was also roaring. The men saw that the bear was the source of the noise and the light.
The men were afraid and hid themselves in the bushes. They saw that the spirits were hunting the bear for a long time but could not catch him. The bear was very strong and the spirits were many but the bear was cunning and he always escaped them. The spirits were angry and they made the thunder and the lightning and they threw their spears and arrows at the bear. They also threw their canoes at him but the bear was too strong and he threw the canoes away and they bounced back to the spirits and hurt many of them. Then the bear ran away into a cave and the spirits could not find him.
The men saw that the spirits were angry and they were going to fight the bear all night. They were going to make a great noise and there would be many lights and many thunders. The men were afraid and they ran away to their camp and hid themselves in their house. They saw that the spirits were going to fight the bear all night and they were going to make a great noise and there would be many lights and many thunders.
In the morning the men went back to their camp and they saw that the spirits were gone. They saw that the bear had gone too. They were happy that they were gone and they were not there to make a noise.

Suddenly a great light was seen over the river and a loud noise was heard. They saw a large object coming across the river, and they could see that it was on fire. The object came down and landed on the shore not far from where the young men were hiding. They were afraid and hid in the bushes. The object was a large canoe filled with Haida men.
The Haida men took out their weapons and started to march inland. One of the young Awa'uws men stepped out from his hiding place and called out to the Haida men in their language. The Haida men were astonished that he could speak their language. They had taken his language from the spirits and had thought that no one on earth knew it. The two young men went to the canoe and saw that the Haida men were carrying strange objects which they had never seen before.
The Haida men took the two young men back to their village to live with them. The young men soon learned all the Haida customs and became Haida men themselves. They were given the names of great chiefs who had lived a long time ago. They took part in all the ceremonies and became great chiefs themselves. They were the only two white men who were ever adopted into the Haida tribe.
One day the two young men wanted to return to their own people. Their friends gave them a big canoe filled with all the things they would need. They set out on their journey and soon came to the village where they were first taken. The Haida men were very happy to see them and gave them many gifts to take back to their own people.
When the two young men reached home their people were very glad to see them. They told their friends and relatives all the things that had happened to them. They lived to be very old and were loved by all their relations. They were the only two white men who ever learned the Haida language and lived to tell about it.

The two men saw a light in the distance and thought it was a fisherman's lantern. They called out to the person and began to row toward the light. As they got closer they realized that the light was not a fisherman's lantern but a canoe full of people. The canoe was adrift because the people in it were frozen, unable to move. The two young men looked in the canoe and saw that all the people in it were dead.

The two men were frightened and didn't know what to do. They took the canoe and the dead people in it and placed them on the shore. Then they took the paddles from the dead people and started to paddle the canoe out to sea. While they were in the middle of the bay they saw a large canoe coming toward them. It was full of people, but as they got closer the two young men saw that these people were all dead also. Then the young men heard a loud noise and the dead people in the canoe began to move and make noises like frogs. The young men were terrified and began to paddle faster.

The large canoe came alongside the smaller one and the dead people from the large canoe climbed into the smaller canoe and pushed the two young men into the water. They swam to the shore and saw that the large canoe had followed them. The people in the large canoe began to dig a pit. Then they lifted the two young men up on the edge of the pit and began to make a fire. The young men were afraid that the people were going to burn them, but the people only wanted to warm themselves.

As they were warming themselves, the people in the large canoe began to make strange noises. The two young men soon realized that the noises were coming from the spirits of the dead people. The spirits were trying to tell them something. The young men watched as the spirits of the dead people rose up out of the canoe and went up into the sky. Then the spirits of the dead people in the large canoe began to fight with the spirits of the dead people in the small canoe.

Suddenly they heard a sound like the rushing of a waterfall, and then they saw a great light in the sky. It was a meteor, and when it hit the water it made a sound like the exploding of a bomb. The young men were very much frightened and hid themselves in the brush until the danger was over. When they came out they saw that the sky was clear again and the meteor gone. They went back to their camp and told their chief what had happened. The chief told them to go and tell the other camps what they had seen. So they went to the other camps and told what had happened.
When the people of the different camps had heard this story they all came together to the place where the meteor had fallen. There they found a hole in the ground covered with stones. They took away the stones and looked down in the hole. At the bottom of the hole they could see water sparkling in the sunlight. They could also see something like a red stone lying at the bottom. They tried to get the stone out but it was too far down. Then the chief said to the men: "You have seen what the Kutuxa has given us. Now we will take the stone out of the hole and place it in our chief's house. We will make a hole in the roof of the house and place the stone there so that the sun can shine down upon it and light up the house."
So they took the stone out of the hole and placed it in their chief's house. Then they placed a log on top of the house and set the stone in the middle of the log. Over the hole where the stone was placed they made a hole in the roof and covered it with skins so that the sunlight could shine down upon the stone. Then they placed the chief's house upon the log and the stone.
The people were very glad and they were all happy. They made a great feast and danced all night long. The old men sang the song of creation and told how the Kutuxa had made the world. When the young men saw this they were very much surprised and asked the old men to tell them more about it. So the old men told them all the stories that they knew about how the world was made and how the people came to be upon the earth.

Suddenly they heard a sound like the roaring of thunder, but it was not thunder, for the sky was clear. They were afraid and hid themselves. They heard the sound again, and then an old man appeared. He said to them, "What are you doing here at this hour?" They said they were from Egulac and had come down to the river to hunt seals. The old man said to them, "You have been tricked by the ghosts of the seals. You should not have come down here at this hour. The ghosts of the seals are angry because their children are being taken from them and turned into articles of clothing. When the ghosts of the seals roar, they are counting the number of seals that have been taken from them. You have interrupted them, and that is why they roared at you. Now go home and never come down here again." The young men went home and never returned to the river to hunt seals again.

From that evening on, the ghosts of the seals roared every night at the same hour. The roar of the ghosts of the seals could be heard for many miles, and people were afraid of it. The roar of the ghosts of the seals was first heard in the year that the smallpox came to the village. The ghosts of the seals were angry because many people had died, and they were taking their children to replace the people who had died. The ghosts of the seals were sad and roared to show their sadness.

The ghosts of the seals roared for many years, and people were afraid of the roar. Some people said that the ghosts of the seals were the spirits of the dead people who had died from the smallpox. The ghosts of the seals were sad because they were alone. The people were afraid of the roar of the ghosts of the seals, and they did not go near the river at night. The ghosts of the seals roared for many years, and then the roar was heard no more.

While they were sitting in their canoe the water began to boil and a great voice was heard saying, "Hurry, get into the canoe, the land is sinking." They did as they were told and when the land surface beneath them collapsed into the water they saw a hole at the edge of the sunken land. A great column of smoke rose from the hole and the men understood that it was the ground's navel. Then the men heard a voice speaking to them and they knew that it was the ground's voice.
The ground's voice told them that a long time ago there had been a great flood that had covered the whole land, and the people had all drowned. The ground's voice said that it had taken in the flood water and saved the people from drowning, but now the people had forgotten the ground and did not pay it any heed. The ground said that it was going to cause a powerful earthquake that would make all the land sink into the water and then the people would know that the ground was the giver of life and sustenance. The ground's voice said that after the earthquake it would rise up again and bring forth new land.
The ground's voice told the men that it was going to send a great wind to sweep across the water. The men saw the wind coming and they saw that it was a powerful and angry wind. The wind swept across the water and the men were knocked down and their canoe was filled with water. The wind was the ground's breath and it was angry because the people would not listen to the ground. The ground's voice told the men to stand up and to hold to the canoe's gunwales. The ground's voice promised to make the wind stop and to make the land rise up once again.
The ground's voice kept its promise and the wind stopped. The land rose up and the men saw that the earthquake and the flood had passed. The ground's voice told the men that they should go back to their camp and tell everyone what had happened. The men did as they were told and when they told the story everyone was amazed. The people knew that the ground was the giver of life and they promised to pay the ground heed in all that they did. From that day on the people lived in peace and the land was good.

Suddenly they heard a sound like the roaring of a mighty waterfall. They listened and then they heard it again. They wondered what it could be and they decided to investigate. They climbed up the steep bank and looked out across the water. It was very still and calm. They saw a large circular object in the distance. They could see what seemed to be a rim and a margin, and in the centre they could see a bright light. They were looking at a full moon, of course, but they had never seen it before and they did not know what it was. They called to their friends and soon there were many young men on the hill calling to their friends and all running towards the water to see the strange object in the distance.
In the morning the old people were puzzled by what had happened. They had never heard of such a thing as a full moon. They decided that the young men had seen a spirit and that the spirit had shown them the full moon. It was a good omen and it meant that the people would have a good year. The young men were pleased to think that they had seen a spirit and that it had shown them something that no one else had seen for a very long time. They felt proud and important.

Narrative
The story begins with two young men from Egulac (a Native American tribe) who go down to the river to hunt seals. It is getting foggy and calm, and while they are there, they hear voices and a great stirring in the water. They think that this might be a spirit coming, so they beach their canoe, set their guns down, and go to the water's edge to look. Suddenly, a great light appears above them, and they see a canoe come out of the water and suspended in the air. In the canoe is a spirit, and the spirit asks them, "Why are you here? What are you looking for?" One of the young men says, "I am looking for a wife, and my companion is looking for a wife also." The spirit says, "I will help you. Get in my canoe." So they get in the canoe, and the spirit takes them to an island where there are many women. The spirit says, "Choose a wife and bring her to this canoe." They choose their wives, get into the canoe, and the spirit takes them back to their village.
